records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: controller actions `addMembers`/`removeMember` call model methods that return Discourse.ajax promises with only `.then()` handlers (group.js shows `.then(function() { self.findMembers(); })` with no `.fail`/`.catch`), and the controller discards the returned promise without any error handling. records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — [P2 confidence=100 advisory] Using `Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json', {` couples membership identity to the draft name bound by `{{text-field name="name" value=name placeholderKey="admin.groups.name_placeholder"}}`, so an administrator editing group A's name to existing group B and then paging or adding a member replaces A's displayed membership/count with B's even though writes still target A through `this.get('id')`; the strongest rebuttal is that names are the public endpoint's established identifier, but independent membership actions now run before Save, so separating draft attributes from persisted identity or using an ID-based read is necessary and eliminates draft-name lookup dependencies from both mutation refreshes and page navigation.
records.rationale: The diff shows findMembers calling Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json') while the admin group form binds the editable name via {{text-field name="name" value=name ...}}. Since addMembers, removeMember, next, and previous all call findMembers using the (possibly unsaved, edited) name while mutations (PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:id) target the id, an unsaved rename causes member reads to hit a different (or nonexistent) group. The mechanism is verifiable directly from the diff, though severity depends on unsaved-name workflow.
